messages:
customer_acct_37: Hey team — starting ~10:30 UTC we saw a spike in 500s and our product started returning much shorter, lower-quality answers. Latency went from ~120ms to >900ms. We think a regional failover happened. Can you confirm which model was served?

maria_support: Sorry about that — I can see increased error rate from your org. Can you paste a request id or example?

customer_acct_37: request_id=rep_2026_03_17_8723, example payload: {"input":"Summarize the quarterly roadmap"} — produced a few token gibberish and then an abrupt end.

robin_infra: @maria_support checking infra events now. There was an automated region fallback for your tenant at 2026-03-17T10:29:45Z from us-west-2 -> eu-central-1 due to capacity pressure. Logging the event: FAILOVER:tenant=acct-37 reason=capacity spike target_region=eu-central-1 policy=latency-first

sre-bot: Incident detected: autoscaler routed 17 requests/s to eu-central-1 pool, 1 fallback swap executed.

dan_runtime: Thanks @robin_infra. Can we get the exact model instance that served the requests? I see in routing logs a fallback to model_id=redwood-medium-quant-eu:v2 from primary redwood-medium:v3 which is not tokenizers-compatible.

olga_ml: That matches a known mismatch: redwood-medium-quant-eu uses a stripped tokenizer (vocab delta) and different EOS handling. If a client keeps the same model id on the request, some token ids will map incorrectly leading to truncated or malformed output.

maria_support: @customer_acct_37 this is likely why outputs were degraded. We're escalating to eng-runtime+ml to confirm and roll a safe fallback. Can you share a minimal repro curl and the model parameter you used?

customer_acct_37: We call POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-medium and stream=false. Quick repro we ran locally (headers redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \ 
  -H "X-Region: us-west-2" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"List next steps for migrating auth flow"}'
```
Response we got: partial tokens then 500, or sometimes short irrelevant answer.

dan_runtime: Action items: (1) pin their tenant routing to us-west-2 for next 24h while we investigate, (2) rotate routes so fallback uses model variant with compatible tokenizer (quant-eu-compat), (3) add a runtime check to reject cross-variant swaps if tokenizer metadata differs.

olga_ml: I'll add a tokenizer-compatibility check in the model registry: compare vocab_hash and special_token_map at load time. If mismatch, treat variant as incompatible for automatic fallback.

robin_infra: Pinned routing for acct-37 to us-west-2 until 2026-03-18T10:30:00Z. Also added a quick metric to alert on 'sudden capability delta' when semantic similarity between primary and served response < 0.6 on the canary prompt set.

maria_support: Noted. @customer_acct_37 we fixed a short-term route pin and will follow up with permanent fix and postmortem. Do you still see errors if you retry now?

customer_acct_37: Retried a couple of calls -> latency back to ~130ms and outputs look normal. Thank you. We'll keep an eye and will send more examples if it recurs.

dan_runtime: Next steps for engineering: create a small reproducer that forces failover to eu-quant variant and run token-by-token compare to detect tokenizer drift. I'll open a ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

olga_ml: Will prepare a test harness and add auto-block for incompatible variant swaps. Estimated PR in 2 days.

maria_support: Closing the immediate support loop. We'll follow up with a written RCA and a scheduled patch. :white_check_mark:

customer_acct_37: Appreciate the quick response :pray:
